title: Add honest lightweight outline fallbacks for unsupported languages

state.decision_rationale: Deferred pending an unsupported-language census and gold range tests. Fallback analysis belongs in a provenance-bearing analyzer layer such as graft, not as unlabeled regex guesses in mktxt.

provenance.source_label: Grok design observation: uneven language outlines
provenance.review_target: MKTCTX/3 Continuum packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: JS, TS, YAML, and Markdown get useful outlines; some files are UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE. That's honest, but over time a lighter fallback, such as top-level headings or export lists, for more languages would increase the value of the outline layer.
feedback.normalized_claim: Provide provenance-labeled lightweight structure for unsupported languages while preserving the distinction from parser-backed outlines.

current_behavior: Graft-backed outlines report available, partial, unsupported, refused, error, or unavailable status.
Unsupported or failed outlines never remove exact selected source.
No regex, heading-only, export-only, or generic fallback analyzer is currently used.

proposal.summary: Evaluate low-cost fallback analyzers whose reduced guarantees are explicit in status, analyzer provenance, and symbol kinds.
candidate_changes: Define fallback statuses distinct from parser-backed available outlines.
Support universally safe structures such as Markdown headings or explicit language export declarations only where grammar is reliable.
Allow pluggable analyzers to contribute outlines with name, version, language, confidence, and partiality.
Measure whether fallbacks improve navigation more than they add false structure.
non_goals: Do not present regex guesses as AST-backed symbols.
Do not let fallback failure remove exact source.
Do not normalize uneven analyzer support into a false complete posture.

questions: Which unsupported languages dominate real packets?
What minimum structure can be extracted with sound ranges for each?
Should fallback records share symbol IDs with future full analyzers?
How should multiple analyzer outputs be reconciled?
risks: Heuristic outlines can create false navigation anchors.
Fallback-generated IDs may churn when a full parser is later introduced.
Analyzer plugins expand supply-chain and reproducibility surfaces.
evidence_needed: Language and unsupported-status census over representative packets.
Gold outline fixtures with range accuracy measurements.
Model navigation tests using unsupported, fallback, and full outlines.
